location.position: East of Downtown Brampton — bordered by Brampton North, East, South, and West neighbourhoods
location.character: Mix of residential, industrial, and commercial areas. Mature, well-established.

demographics.note: Most European-origin neighbourhood in this study — Canadian 21%, English 19%, Scottish 14%, Irish 14%. 17% seniors. 21% single-person households. Very different character from other Brampton neighbourhoods.

home_types.notes: Oldest housing stock of all neighbourhoods in this study — 93% of homes built before 1980. Peel Village and Eldomar Heights are classic 1950s-60s subdivisions with bungalows, splits, and 2-storeys. 14% high-rise apartments is notable — more housing diversity than typical Brampton suburb.

market_data.zolo_note: Zolo has two zones: 'Brampton East' (historic area near downtown, $808K) and 'Bram East' (northeast, $1,087,934) — very different areas. This is the historic Brampton East.
market_data.honestdoor_note: HonestDoor avg $460K likely reflects condo/apartment units pulling down the average. Detached homes considerably higher.
market_data.note: At $808K avg (Zolo), Brampton East is ~9% below the Brampton-wide average of $884K — reflecting older stock but still strong demand for established neighbourhood.
sources: zolo.ca Brampton East trends May 2026 — $808,708 avg

parks_and_recreation.western_boundary_feature: Etobicoke Creek corridor — parklands and trail form western boundary of neighbourhood
parks_and_recreation.note: 3 trails plus Etobicoke Creek corridor = notable trail connectivity for a mature urban neighbourhood

character_notes.oldest_area: 93% of homes built before 1980 — oldest housing stock in this study. Bungalows, side-splits, and 2-storeys from the Peel Village / Eldomar Heights era.
character_notes.european_origin: Most European-origin neighbourhood in Brampton's suburban areas — Canadian, English, Scottish, Irish, Portuguese. Very different feel from newer South Asian-dominant areas.
character_notes.aging_population: 17% of residents are 65+ — notably higher than Brampton average. 21% single-person households. This neighbourhood has long-term residents who have aged in place.
character_notes.most_affordable: At ~$808K avg, this is the most affordable established neighbourhood in this study (vs. $901K Northwood Park, $1.31M Castlemore).
character_notes.apartment_presence: 14% high-rise apartment = more housing type diversity. Entry-level units available for first-time buyers or investors.
character_notes.industrial_mix: Neighbourhood includes industrial and commercial areas — not purely residential. Relevant for buyers expecting a suburb-only feel.
